claim: Degradation matters mainly in the gut and portal bed rather than systemically

claim: The hepatic vagal response to intraportal GLP-1 uses a receptor not engaged by exendin-4 and not blocked by exendin(9-39)
caveat: argues AGAINST agonist engagement of the portal route; receptor never molecularly identified; anaesthetised rats, 2000; never repeated with a long-acting agonist

claim: The hepatoportal vagal branch is not required for GLP-1's incretin or intake-suppressing effects; paracrine GI vagal afferents are
caveat: animal; refines and partly contradicts the portal hypothesis

claim: Circulating GLP-1 can suppress food intake without vagal afferents
caveat: animal; counter-evidence to the vagal hypothesis

claim: Intact vagal innervation is required for exogenous GLP-1 to reduce food intake in humans
caveat: 20 men, surgical truncal vagotomy + pyloroplasty, native GLP-1 not an agonist, no body-weight endpoint; pyloroplasty confounds emptying

claim: Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy is present in 18.6% of patients at T2D diagnosis
caveat: a cardiovascular proxy, not a measure of the gastrointestinal afferent limb

claim: Reported CAN prevalence ranges from about 2.5% to as high as 90% depending on tests and cohort
caveat: review; the upper figure refers to type 1 diabetes. The doc's '20-40% in known disease' was NOT verified and is not used

claim: Vagal myelinated fibre loss is documented post mortem in diabetes
caveat: TYPE 1 diabetes, n=5, established clinical autonomic failure. The doc described this as 'individuals with diabetes'; transfer to T2D trial populations is limited

claim: Diabetic mice show structural peripheral nerve changes including the vagus
caveat: db/db mice; vagal changes appeared LATE relative to other nerves

claim: Gut glucose sensing and enteric/vagal afferent activation are impaired in a type 2 diabetes model
caveat: UCD-T2DM RATS, not mice as stated in the source document; no agonist given; no weight endpoint

claim: Portal GLP-1 receptor density and afferent glucose responsiveness are reduced in insulin-resistant obese animals
caveat: reduction was between the SPLENIC VEIN and the entrance of the liver, not 'porta hepatis and left gastric vein' as stated in the source document; species not stated in the abstract

claim: Intragastric glucose signalling to the hypothalamus requires GLP-1 receptor signalling and is abolished by high-fat feeding
caveat: the receptor dependence demonstrated was CENTRAL (central exendin(9-39), Glp1r-KO), not portal; c-Fos colocalised with arcuate NPY neurons; animal

claim: Agonist-induced anorexia is blunted in a dysmetabolic rodent host alongside nodose GLP-1 receptor downregulation and reduced ileal L-cell number
caveat: the only identified study testing an agonist alongside peripheral changes; diet-induced obesity model not diabetes; short-acting agonist; acute intake endpoint

claim: Gastric emptying in diabetes referred for upper GI symptoms is more often accelerated than delayed
caveat: referral population with symptoms; not population-representative

claim: Oral semaglutide bioavailability does not differ significantly between healthy participants and people with T2D
caveat: population PK model; within-subject variability in bioavailability is high (137%) but falls to 33% at steady state

claim: Background metformin raises endogenous GLP-1 and alters the intestinal bile acid pool and microbiome
caveat: review; no quantification, and no study has tested whether background metformin modifies weight response to an incretin agonist

claim: NTS preproglucagon neurons form a secondary satiation circuit and are not required for basal intake or weight regulation
caveat: animal

claim: No study has measured endogenous incretin secretion, DPP-4 activity or autonomic function as predictors of weight response to an incretin agonist in either population
